courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Undergraduate Research Experience
courses.description: Supervised undergraduate directed research on communication science topics of mutual interest to the student and a faculty member.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 12 total completions.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Autism in Our Communities: An Interdisciplinary Perspective
courses.description: Students have 30 hours of service-learning with individuals with autism at community partner sites. Class discussions introduce students to diverse topics related to autism spectrum disorder. This is an APPLES course.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: American Sign Language I
courses.description: This American Sign Language (ASL) course includes topics on linguistic features, cultural protocols, and core vocabulary for students to function in basic ASL conversations on a variety of topics. All instructions and discussions in the classroom will be conducted in ASL. Students minoring in Speech and Hearing Sciences have priority in registering.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: American Sign Language II
courses.description: Students in the Speech and Hearing Minor have priority in registering. The American Sign Language (ASL) course focuses on developing conversational skills on a variety of topics. All instructions and discussions in the classroom will be conducted in ASL.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Introduction to Communication Disorders
courses.description: Introductory overview of communication disorders, including the nature of communication across the lifespan; cultural and linguistic issues that impact communication; communication modalities; speech disorders; language disorders; hearing disorders; swallowing disorders.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Human Communication Across the Lifespan
courses.description: Development of human communication processes across the lifespan, including linguistic and cultural bases of communication.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Human Communication Across the Lifespan (EE)
courses.description: Development of human communication processes across the lifespan, including linguistic and cultural bases of communication. Includes a minimum of 30 service hours related to human communication. 12 spaces reserved for Juniors in Speech and Hearing Sciences Minor.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Introduction to Phonetics
courses.description: A detailed study of the International Phonetic Alphabet with emphasis on the sound system of American English. Application of phonetics to problems of pronunciation and articulation. Includes broad and narrow phonetic transcription.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Speech Science
courses.description: Introduction to the science of speech, including production, acoustics, and perception.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Speech, Language, and Hearing Mechanisms
courses.description: Anatomy and physiology of the speech producing and aural mechanisms.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Introductory Audiology I
courses.description: Theory and practice of the measurement of hearing, causative factors in hearing loss, evaluation of audiometric results, and demonstration of clinical procedures.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Introduction to Clinical Practice in Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology
courses.description: Introduction to diagnosis and treatment of communication disorders, including articulation, fluency, voice, and language, and those resulting from autism and hearing loss.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Introduction to Research in Speech and Hearing
courses.description: Required preparation, statistics course. Experimental and descriptive research designs in speech and hearing sciences, including both group and single subject.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Clinical Practicum in Audiology
courses.description: Supervised clinical experience in Audiology which covers the breadth of the scope of practice. This course is taken multiple semesters throughout the AuD program.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Cochlear Implants: Foundations & Clinical Applications
courses.description: Examines fundamentals of cochlear implants, candidacy, evaluation, equipment, programming, and performance outcomes.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Audiologic Assessment
courses.description: Clinical Audiology assessment including pure-tone audiometry, immittance measures, and other measures commonly employed in the standard diagnostic battery.
requisites_notes: could not interpret: 'Prerequisite, SPHS 582 or equivalent' (unrecognized text: 'equivalent')

source.text: SPHS 710. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, SPHS 582 or equivalent.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Audiologic Assessment Lab
courses.description: Laboratory exercises in threshold determination, clinical masking and speech recognition testing, all concepts introduced in SPHS 710 , Audiologic Assessment.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Characteristics of Amplification Systems
courses.description: Amplification options for the hearing-impaired; specifically, hearing aid, electroacoustics, and earmold technologies. Additionally, hearing aid selection procedures are presented.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Characteristics of Amplification Lab
courses.description: Laboratory activities related to earmolds, hearing aids, and ANSI electroacoustic verification.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Anatomy and Physiology of Hearing
courses.description: This course will cover anatomy and physiology of the peripheral hearing system (outer, middle, and inner ear) as well as relevant central pathways.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Professional Considerations in Speech and Hearing
courses.description: To provide the student with information about current issues facing professionals. Issues include changing delivery systems, leadership, treatment efficacy and quality, reimbursement, and ethics.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Auditory Perception
courses.description: This course provides an overview of psychoacoustics - the psychology of hearing. Content includes introductory acoustics, normal sound perception, and the perceptual consequences of impaired hearing.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Hearing Disorders
courses.description: Diseases and disorders of the auditory system and their management.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Clinical Issues and Experiences in Audiology
courses.description: Online course in Year One, In-Person Course Years Two and Three, this course covers universal precautions, privacy regulations, report writing, clinical practice with diverse cultural groups, ethical considerations, coding and billing, and other aspects of audiology practice.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Instrumentation and Calibration
courses.description: Principles of instrumentation relevant to clinical practice including study of electronics, filters, and analog and digital processing.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Auditory Strategies for Spoken Language in Deaf Children
courses.description: Instruction and application of a variety of topics demonstrating the use of auditory techniques, and strategies to promote the use of spoken language in children with hearing loss.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Principles of Prevention, Assessment, and Intervention in Speech-Pathology
courses.description: Principles and methods of prevention, assessment, and intervention for people with communication and swallowing disorders, including consideration of anatomical/physiological, psychological, developmental, and linguistic and cultural correlates of the disorders.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Neuroanatomy
courses.description: A survey of neurological anatomy in relation to clinical speech-pathology and audiology. Topics include organization of the CNS, neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, and neurochemistry.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Aphasia
courses.description: Discussion of adult aphasia and its clinical management, including assessment, diagnosis, prognosis, counseling, and treatment. Combined lectures and laboratories.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Pediatric Speech Disorders
courses.description: Identification and differential diagnosis of delayed and disordered speech development; associated body structures and functions; intervention approaches focused on improving speech intelligibility, fluency, and participation in communication activities.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, SPHS 530; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: SPHS 743. | 4 Credits. | Prerequisite, SPHS 530 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Motor Speech Disorders
courses.description: Assessment and treatment of adults with disorders of motor speech control (i.e. dysarthria, anarthria, fluency, and apraxia of speech).

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Cognitive Communication Disorders Across the Lifespan
courses.description: An advanced course on cognitive bases of human communication and cognitive-communication disorders. Topics covered include theoretical models of cognitive communication across the lifespan, cognitive processes thought to underlie communication, and common clinical presentations of cognitive communication disorders associated with traumatic brain injury, right hemisphere injury, left hemisphere stroke and dementia. The goal of this course is to improve students abilities to apply theoretical models of communication and current research literature to assessment and practice. Restricted to: Speech-Language Pathology Graduate students in the MS-SLP program.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Voice Disorders
courses.description: Assessment and management of a range of laryngeal and aerodigestive disorders across the lifespan. Students admitted to the Master of Science in Speech and Hearing Sciences/Speech-language pathology program only.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Evaluation and Clinical Management of Persons with Oral-Facial Anomalies
courses.description: In-depth analysis of the embryologic and physiologic bases of oral-facial anomalies and the team approach to assessment and habilitation. Particular emphasis placed upon the following specialties: genetics, plastic surgery, prosthodontics, orthodontics, otolaryngology, and speech-language pathology.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Global Issues and Practices in Communication Disorders
courses.description: Examination and discussion of issues related to international practices in communication sciences and disorders, including effective global engagement. Restricted to: MS/SLP Graduate students and advanced undergraduates in the Minor with permission of instructor.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Seminar in Medical Speech Language Pathology
courses.description: Discussion of normal aging and language. Assessment and treatment of cognitive and linguistic problems in persons with dementing conditions, right hemisphere dysfunction, and traumatic brain injury.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Dysphagia
courses.description: Discussion of the development of the normal swallow, anatomy and physiology of the swallowing mechanism, and assessment and team management of swallowing disorders.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Neurologic Communication Disorders in Adults
courses.description: Overview of communication disorders commonly seen in adult populations. These include disorders of language, cognition, speech and motor control, voice, and fluency.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Child Communication Disorders
courses.description: Disorders of child speech and language development, as a prerequisite for advanced specialized coursework and supervised clinical practicum.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Language Impairments in School Age Children
courses.description: Assessment and intervention methods for receptive and expressive language (phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics, prelinguistic communication, and paralinguistic communication) in speaking, listening, reading, and writing.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Augmentative and Alternative Communication
courses.description: Introduction to Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) systems for individuals with complex communication impairments; processes involved in selecting, representing, and organizing vocabulary; strategies to support development of communicative competence in AAC.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Supervised Clincal Experience in Speech-Language Pathology I
courses.description: Supervised clinical experience in Speech-Language Pathology scope of practice.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Supervised Clinical Experience in Speech-Language Pathology II
courses.description: Supervised clinical experience in Speech-Language Pathology scope of practice.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Supervised Clinical Experience in Speech-Language Pathology III
courses.description: Supervised clinical experience in Speech-Language Pathology scope of practice.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Supervised Clinical Experience in Speech-Language Pathology IV
courses.description: Supervised clinical experience in Speech-Language Pathology scope of practice.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Supervised Clinical Experience in Speech-Language Pathology V
courses.description: Supervised clinical experience in Speech-Language Pathology scope of practice.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Ethical Practice Policies and Guidelines
courses.description: Academic program accreditation standards; standards of ethical conduct; practice policies and guidelines; prevention of communication disorders; role of the speech-language pathologist.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Contemporary Professional Issues in Education
courses.description: Principles and rules of the current ASHA Code of Ethics; technical reports, diagnostic and treatment reports; treatment plans, and professional correspondence.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Professional Development In Person-Centered Care
courses.description: Program coordinator may give permission for students to take this course. Tenets of person- and family-centered care, consistent with recognized standards of ethical practice and in accordance with applicable state and federal laws. Includes discussion of barriers and facilitators that impact access to and utilization of speech-language pathology services in education and health care settings.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Professional Practice Issues in Speech-Language Pathology
courses.description: Cultural competence; conflict management; effective clinical and professional interaction with clients/patients and relevant others.
requisites_notes: comma-separated list without a conjunction was read as AND
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 3 total completions.

source.text: SPHS 779. | 2 Credits. | Prerequisites, SPHS 776 , SPHS 777 , SPHS 778 .

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Pediatric Dysphagia
courses.description: This course will cover content on the specialty area of pediatric dysphagia assessment and intervention. The course will cover normal development of feeding skills, explore underlying etiologies of feeding disorders, current methods and philosophies of providing evaluation and intervention, existing and ongoing research in these areas, and special populations such as infants with craniofacial anomalies.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Problems in Speech and Hearing Sciences
courses.description: May be repeated for credit.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Audiologic Rehabilitation for Children
courses.description: Covers speech perception and the effects of hearing loss on perception and production of speech as background for understanding assessment and treatment, with an auditory-verbal emphasis. Pediatric assessment and amplification are reviewed.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Audiologic Rehabilitation for Adults
courses.description: Theoretical bases and history of audiologic rehabilitation of adults. Also, practical approaches to assessment and therapeutic intervention are presented. The roles of assistive technology and family-based counseling are included.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Seminar in Early Intervention
courses.description: Stages of communication development of children from birth to five years old; clinical issues related to the assessment tools and intervention and planning for children with disabilities and their families.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Seminar in Audiologic Rehabilitation
courses.description: Audiologic rehabilitation including counseling, visual speech perception, auditory training, special needs of older adults and psychosocial aspects of hearing loss will be addressed. Review of technology to enhance communication included.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Introduction to Cochlear Implants
courses.description: Introductory information regarding cochlear implant candidacy, an overview of implant components, the evaluation process, surgery, device programming, and initiation of post implantation therapy. Class meets three hours for five weeks.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Pediatric Audiology
courses.description: Clinical procedures used in the identification and management of hearing loss in young children.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Pediatric Amplification and Assistive Listening Devices
courses.description: This course covers prescriptive formulas, verification and fitting of hearing aids and FM systems, and suggested monitoring of progress when working with young children with hearing loss and their families.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Fitting and Dispensing of Amplification Systems
courses.description: Theoretical and practical approaches to fitting amplification systems and the procedures for dispensing amplification systems to the hearing-impaired.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Fitting and Dispensing of Amplification Lab
courses.description: Laboratory experiences related to the selection, programming, and fitting of amplification devices to hearing impaired individuals.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Auditory Evoked Potentials I
courses.description: This course explores the field of auditory evoked responses. The primary focus is on responses from the auditory periphery including otoacoustic emissions (OAEs), electrocochleography (ECochG), and the auditory brainstem response (ABR).

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: The Auditory Evoked Potentials I Lab
courses.description: Elecrophysiologic laboratory exercises to accompany Auditory Evoked Potentials I course.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Auditory Evoked Potentials II
courses.description: The primary focus of this course is to cover auditory evoked potentials (Auditory Steady State Responses [ASSR] and Cortical Auditory Evoked Potentials [CAEP]) in addition to the ABR.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Occupational and Community Audiology
courses.description: Military and industrial audiology and hearing conservation, including physiological and psychological factors.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Balance Assessment and Rehabilitation
courses.description: Principles of vestibular function and dysfunction, clinical assessment, and management.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Balance Assessment Lab
courses.description: Laboratory exercises to accompany Balance Assessment course. To include case history, bedside examination, and objective measurements.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Educational Audiology
courses.description: Examines the provision of services to school-age children, with special focus on eligibility determination and assessment of central auditory perception.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Business Management and Professional Issues
courses.description: Examine healthcare and business models that impact audiology practice. Personnel management, marketing, quality assurance, and service reimbursement for audiology practices will be covered.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Audiology Grand Rounds
courses.description: Examines clinical cases from the perspective of presenting symptoms, test results, and clinical outcomes.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Embryology and Genetics of Hearing and Deafness
courses.description: Genetics related to developing hearing and balance structures as well as syndromic and nonsyndromic hearing loss and deafness.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Pharmacology & Tinnitus in Audiology Practice
courses.description: Advanced audiology course that provides fundamental knowledge about pharmacological mechanisms and their impact on hearing and balance, as well as evaluation and management of patients with persistent tinnitus.

source.text: SPHS 827. | 2 Credits. | Prerequisite, SPHS 715 and SPHS 725 .

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: This course gives enrolled graduate students in the curriculum an opportunity to pursue research supervised by one or more faculty members, culminating in a written document or special project.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Advanced Signal Processing
courses.description: This course will provide information regarding advanced signal processing utilized in digital amplification and cochlear implants.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Speech Acoustics
courses.description: This course provides information on the fundamentals of speech production, including the acoustic characteristics of normal and disordered speech.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: This is the foundation course in a series related to providing services to children with hearing loss. Six units focus on working with families, speech acoustics, audiological interpretation, instrumentation, foundations of speech and language, and early literacy.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Counseling and Communication Disorders
courses.description: This course provides a broad overview of contemporary counseling issues in communication disorders. The impact of subject age, life course, and cultural background on interviewing and counseling is included.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Audiology Interpretation and Hearing Technologies
courses.description: This course focuses on behavioral and physiologic assessment of hearing in children and how these measures are used in aural habilitation. Fundamentals of hearing instrument technology including the selection and fitting of hearing aids and cochlear implants are addressed.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Aging and Communication Disorders
courses.description: This course focuses on medical, psychological, and social theories and aspects of aging as they relate to communication processes and disorders.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Seminar in Speech-Language Pathology
courses.description: Special topics and significant literature in the field of speech pathology.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Fluency Disorders
courses.description: Course participants will develop an understanding of evaluation and treatment of acquired and developmental fluency disorders in children and adults through lecture and hands-on practice.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Language Disorders Encountered in Audiology
courses.description: Students will learn about four areas of language disorders affecting children and adults (receptive and expressive language disorders, communication modalities, social aspects of communication, and cognitive aspects of communication) through readings, posted videos, and online quizzes. This is an asynchronous online course.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Speech Disorders Encountered in Audiology
courses.description: Students will learn about speech disorders (fluency, voice, articulation, and craniofacial anomalies) through readings, posted videos, and online quizzes. This is an online asynchronous course.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Speech and Language Disorders Encountered in Audiology
courses.description: Students will select two topics from speech disorders (fluency, voice, articulation, and craniofacial anomalies) and two topics from language disorders (receptive and expressive language disorders, communication modalities, social aspects of communication, and cognitive aspects of communication). This is an online asynchronous course with readings, videos, and quizzes.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Seminar in Language and Language Disorders
courses.description: Special topics and significant literature in the field of language and language disorders. May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Listening and Spoken Language Development and Intervention
courses.description: The course focuses on typical development, impact of hearing loss on listening and spoken language acquisition, assessment, strategies/techniques, and intervention for children birth-5 years who are deaf/hard of hearing.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Speech and Language Impairments of Children
courses.description: Seminar course exploring categorical classifications of young children and the impact of these categories on assessment and intervention. Common topics include autism, visual impairments, fragile X syndrome, and Down syndrome.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Directed Research Experience
courses.description: Individual work by a student (supervised by faculty) to explore an area of interest in a research paper or guided research experience.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Teaching and Supervision
courses.description: Course regarding teaching of skills and supervision of individuals conducting screening programs. Introduction to teaching and development of assessment tools provides a background for the teaching lab associated with this course.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Autism Seminar
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to develop a familiarity and understanding of topics related to Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD). Issues related to characteristics, etiologies, theories, assessment, and intervention will be discussed.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Seminar in Speech Science
courses.description: Advanced special topics and current research in speech science. May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Autism and Other Developmental Disabilities in Children Who Are Deaf or Hard of Hearing I
courses.description: Students will acquire knowledge related to screening, diagnosis, and intervention for children who have autism and/or other developmental disabilities in addition to hearing loss.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Autism and Other Developmental Disabilities in Children Who Are Deaf or Hard of Hearing II
courses.description: Students and faculty will examine challenges and solutions related to screening, diagnosis, and intervention for children who have autism and/or other developmental disabilities in addition to hearing loss.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 2 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: North Carolina Service Learning Trip
courses.description: Interdisciplinary learning experience focused on examining social determinants of health while performing service activities in collaboration with community partners.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Autism Seminar
courses.description: Participants develop knowledge of the major neuropsychological theories of autism and methodological issues in autism research through reading and discussion of literature; participate in developing and presenting autism research projects individually or in groups.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Literacy
courses.description: This course provides an overview of literacy development for children birth to eight years old. It will also address the impact of hearing loss on the development of literacy.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Research Design
courses.description: Doctoral seminar that introduces the student to principles of quantitative research methodology.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Seminar in Single Subject and Survey Research
courses.description: Doctoral student seminar that introduces the student to principles of single subject and survey research methodology.

courses.subject: SPHS
courses.title: Research in the Context of the Evidence-Based Practice Movement in Early Intervention
courses.description: Overview of the evidence-based practice (EBP) movement in early intervention (EI), definitions of EBP, systems for appraising evidence quality, examination of evidence base for current practices in EI.
